First of all, it won't happen.

That aside, California would have to duplicate all the of the existing federal functions they deem necessary. They would need their own state department to negotiate trade and other agreements with other nations; their own military; their own social security, medicaid, and medicare. Their own EPA, FAA, FDA, and don't forget, their own central bank... it would be tremendously expensive.

Sure, they would save some money - the difference between what they currently pay to the feds, and what they currently receive - but that would be a tiny fraction of these tremendous new costs. And don't forget, California is flat broke. They can't even pay the pensions they have promised.

Which brings the next problem to light... their currency would not be particularly strong. They import most of their energy, much of their water, and most of the physical products they use day to day, and they would be trying to pay for all this with a weak Cali-Dollar. If they are broke now, they would be totally buried shortly thereafter.

The impact on the US? Assuming we negotiate continued access to the military bases, and negotiate trade deals and a fairly porous boarder, we'd hardly miss them. We'd take a modest financial hit, and of course we'd probably never elect a democrat president again for the foreseeable future. But we'd go on a lot better than they would.

California like to talk about how they have Silicon Valley and Hollywood to fund their tax-base, as well as how they are a "Donor State" (The fact that they pay more to the Feds in taxes than they take, in funding from the same Feds) as reasons they would be self-sufficient. But let's examine this for a bit, shall we?

As it currently stands, both Silicon Valley and Hollywood receive massive amounts of funding and grants from the United States Government. Battleship received a ton of support from the US Navy, GI Jane received lots of support, input, and funding from the US Army, and Top Gun got the same from the US Air Force, to name three films that immediately come to mind when considering Hollywood getting support from the US Government. If California secedes, this effectively means that those film companies will no longer be "US Entities" and the US Government will have no reason to help support them to push film pieces helpful to US Government interests. They can kiss that sweet funding goodbye...unless they return to the city that was Hollywood before Hollywood was a thing. People forget that California wasn't always the Film Production Capitol of the nation, that New York was once the film-creation-central of the nation before obscenity laws drove them and the pornographers out West. Because of all the sweet support from Uncle Sam, they've been able to soak the costs of California's obscene taxation rates. But without all that support, and without the support of their fellow citizens across the nation that was once their homeland, they're not going to survive very long. Especially considering the MPAA's demographic-marketing research showing that in the past several years, the largest population to support the Silver Screen industries was Caucasians, the demographic Cali is most trying to rid itself of, combined with the fact that they did so at almost twice the rate of the next-most-supportive demographic, the Hispanics...and it doesn't look so hot for any movie industry that stays in Cali.

I suspect the demographics to be similar with Silicon Valley. Fact remains, it's the Caucasians that have the money, and the Caucasians that buy these products, and thus Caucasians that support these industries. Chase off the Caucasians, and you chase off your primary market demographic, ensuring a slow-starvation death of your industry, even in a best-case scenario.

Then consider also that California's roads are considered the worst in the nation, outside of DC, thus making their roads the worst state in the nation for road maintenance (I think the last figure I checked was somewhere around $80 Billion in deferred maintenance costs that are due). Under this guise, the idea of them being a "Donor Nation" suddenly isn't so appealing, because it means they are turning down funds they could use to repair vital infrastructure that very badly needs it...and it's just going to get worse, and thus more expensive to fix, the longer they wait to fix it. They're not being responsible by being a "Donor State", they're starving their infrastructure for bragging rights. And where are they going to get all of this money to fix up their roads, bridges and other vital infrastructure after they secede, Silicon Valley and Hollywood? Oh wait, they're going to be planning on preserving their commercial interests, which means likely moving back to New York or the Washington State/DC Areas (in the case of Silicon Valley). The difference in taxation rates, combined with the support from Uncle Sam alone would be incentive enough to draw them out of the People's Republic of California.

Then there's their pension crisis. California's public pensions are underfunded massively. Like, to the point if it were all to come due today, it would bankrupt them several times over. More specifically, they're underfunded to the tune of almost a Trillion dollars. Where are they going to get the money to fulfill these obligations, if they secede? They already can't pay now, and are doing everything they can to keep the shell game going for as long as possible.

For the US, it likely just continue to be business as usual. The DNC would face it's utter death, as their biggest bloc of support (California's guaranteed 55 Blue Electoral College votes) would be excised from the rest of the nation, so excising this cancer would actually be a good thing, for us. But California needs us to absorb the impact of their foolhardy policies much more than we need them. Silicon Valley hasn't innovated much in the realm of concrete products for at least two decades. All the new shit coming out is just improvements on current tech. Hollywood has stagnated to the point of snowballing downhill, trying to cash in on Nostalgia-factor rather than taking risks with anything. If they secede, those industry giants will jump ship, if just to save themselves. California will make a lot of noise, but I doubt they will follow through...because they'd be punching holes in their own rubber raft whilst out at sea, just to spite the folks that threw it to them, if they did.

tl;dr - California needs us more than we need them, and a secession would help us more than hurt us. If anything, it would lead to California's insolvency even before you take immigration into account.
